questions.question: What aspect of fMRI BOLD timing motivates using a bidirectional rather than conventional unidirectional LSTM?

options.A: Future temporal context can help model variable BOLD latency without explicit delay adjustment
options.B: Past context is unavailable in fMRI, so only future volumes can be used
options.C: BOLD responses are instantaneous, so bidirectional processing removes spatial features
options.D: The stimulus timing is unknown, so the network must infer the number of subjects

questions.rationale: The method uses both past and future temporal context to capture BOLD dynamics without applying the conventional estimated-delay correction.
questions.evidence_quote: Because of the variations in latency of the BOLD responses across time, we assert that the temporal context from future is also important

questions.question: How were the HCP working-memory states defined, including the control and fixation labels?

options.A: Eight combinations of four stimuli and 0-/2-back, plus fixation as a ninth 'others' state
options.B: Four stimulus states only, with 0-back and 2-back collapsed and fixation excluded
options.C: Two states, 0-back versus 2-back, with stimulus identity used only as a covariate
options.D: Nine states corresponding to nine cortical lobes, with fixation treated as background

questions.rationale: The task crosses four stimulus categories with two load conditions and treats fixation periods as 'others,' yielding nine states.
questions.evidence_quote: time instants belonging to the fixation blocks were labelled as "others", yielding a total of S = 9 brain states.

questions.question: What input dimensionality and sequence length were used after cortical parcellation?
questions.rationale: Averaging voxels within 360 cortical ROIs produced a 360-by-405 tensor for each scan.
questions.evidence_quote: The generated 405 time-points sequence of 360 ROIs were structured in a 360 by 405 2D-tensor.

questions.question: What combination schemes for forward and backward hidden activations were compared?

options.A: Concatenation, element-wise addition, and element-wise averaging
options.B: Concatenation, max pooling, and attention-weighted summation
options.C: Addition, recurrent gating, and temporal convolution
options.D: Averaging, matrix multiplication, and majority voting

questions.rationale: The paper labels the three alternatives bi-LSTM-c, bi-LSTM-a, and bi-LSTM-µ for concatenation, addition, and averaging.
questions.evidence_quote: The three possible ways of combining the activations are vector concatenation (bi-LSTM-c), element-wise vector addition (bi-LSTM-a), and element-wise averaging (bi-LSTM-µ).

questions.question: How did the backward LSTM compute its activation at time t?

options.A: Using future temporal dependency from the activation at t+1
options.B: Using only the current activation and the forward cell state at t−1
options.C: Reversing the labels while retaining the ordinary past dependency
options.D: Averaging all hidden activations from the entire sequence

questions.rationale: The reverse-direction pass uses the future dependency h at t+1 to compute its backward hidden activation.
questions.evidence_quote: The backward hidden activation ←h t l is calculated by using the future temporal dependency h t +1 l.

questions.question: What architecture and training window were used in the main bi-LSTM comparison?

options.A: Two 256-unit LSTM layers and a 9-neuron output layer, trained on 40-point windows with 10-point overlap
options.B: Three 256-unit LSTM layers and a 4-neuron output layer, trained on 10-point windows with 40-point overlap
options.C: Two 360-unit LSTM layers and a 9-neuron output layer, trained on non-overlapping 405-point sequences
options.D: A single 256-unit layer and 9-neuron output, trained on 32-point windows with 8-point overlap

questions.rationale: The model used two bi-LSTM layers of 256 hidden activations, nine state outputs, and sliding windows of width 40 with overlap 10.
questions.evidence_quote: two hidden bi-LSTM layers with each LSTM cell having 256 hidden activations

questions.question: How was inter-subject cross-validation organized for the 400 participants?

options.A: Ten folds, with 360 participants for development and 40 held out for evaluation in each fold
options.B: Four folds, with 300 participants for training and 100 for testing
options.C: Ten folds, with 40 participants used for training and 360 for testing
options.D: A random 80/20 split of time points within each participant, without held-out subjects

questions.rationale: The design held out one of ten participant groups of 40 and developed the model on the other 360 participants.
questions.evidence_quote: Data from N = 400 participants was divided into 10 parts, of which 9 parts (N = 360 subjects) were kept for model development and the remaining one part (N = 40 subjects) was kept unseen for evaluating the model performance.

questions.question: What class-imbalance strategy was used because fixation-derived 'others' observations were more numerous?

options.A: Class weights from compute_class_weight were applied inversely proportional to class frequency
options.B: The 'others' samples were discarded before training
options.C: The minority task states were oversampled to match 'others' exactly
options.D: A separate binary classifier was trained for each stimulus category

questions.rationale: The authors estimated weights using sklearn's compute_class_weight and applied inverse-frequency weighting in the loss.
questions.evidence_quote: weights for the imbalanced classes were estimated using Sklearn's "compute_class_weight" [15] routine and were applied during loss function calculation

questions.question: What were the reported overall accuracies for unidirectional LSTM and concatenating bi-LSTM, respectively?
questions.rationale: The results report a higher and less variable accuracy for bi-LSTM-c than for the conventional LSTM.
questions.evidence_quote: The overall accuracy of the unidirectional LSTM model was 0.66 ± 0.18, whereas the classification accuracy of the bidirectional LSTM (bi-LSTM-c) was 0.84 ± 0.02.

questions.question: Which limitations or future-work directions did the authors identify despite the improved decoding?

options.A: Tune window length/overlap, improve class-imbalance handling, and investigate body–tools confusion
options.B: Add BOLD delay correction, reduce the number of ROIs, and eliminate future context
options.C: Replace the HCP task with resting state and remove dropout
options.D: Increase the number of classes and use unweighted loss for fixation

questions.rationale: The conclusion names fixed windowing, residual imbalance and body–tools confusion as follow-up issues.
questions.evidence_quote: future work may involve tuning the window-size and overlap for time-series chunking. The problem of class imbalance, although, majorly handled, still requires more sophisticated handling.
